description: Establish the baseline and scaffold the backend project so the server can reuse the frontend's pure domain code. First confirm the existing frontend is green (install, test, build, typecheck), verify the local Postgres-via-Docker path works, then create a server/ package (Node + TypeScript + Fastify) that imports the existing src/domain modules (gift.ts, selectors.ts, types.ts, products.ts, ids.ts) rather than duplicating them. This feature leaves a compiling, testable skeleton with a Postgres helper script and a health endpoint; no business endpoints yet.
steps: At repo root run `npm ci` then `npm test` (expect 61 passing across 4 files), `npm run build`, and `npm run typecheck` to capture the green baseline. Record the results.
Create a feature branch (e.g. `feat/backend`) from main. Do NOT stage or commit the untracked .kiro/ directory at any point.

Verify the Postgres path: `docker run --name hello-talk-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -e POSTGRES_DB=hello_talk -p 5432:5432 -d postgres:16-alpine` starts, then `docker exec hello-talk-pg pg_isready` succeeds. Note that the `docker compose` plugin is NOT available — use plain `docker run`. Create `server/scripts/db.sh` (or db.mjs) that starts/stops/resets this container so dev and tests share one command.

Create server/ with its own package.json ("type":"module"), TypeScript (strict, matching the root tsconfig style: ES2022, moduleResolution NodeNext or bundler, verbatimModuleSyntax), Fastify, a Postgres client (pg or postgres), and vitest as devDependency. Add scripts: dev, build (tsc emit to server/dist), typecheck (tsc --noEmit), test (vitest run).

Set up domain code reuse: the server must consume src/domain/gift.ts, selectors.ts, types.ts, products.ts, ids.ts WITHOUT copying them. Use a TypeScript path mapping / project reference / relative import from server/ up into ../src/domain, and make the server's tsconfig include those files so they compile under the server build. Confirm importing checkGiftAction/applyGiftAction, directChatBetween, unreadCount, normalizeCode, findUserByCode, productById, newGiftOrder, and the Db/User/GiftOrder types works from server code. Note: ids.ts uses Web Crypto (crypto.getRandomValues/randomUUID) which exists on Node 22 global crypto — verify newId()/newFriendCode() run under Node.

Add a Fastify server entry (server/src/index.ts) with a GET /health endpoint returning {status:'ok'} and configuration via env vars (PORT, DATABASE_URL, COOKIE_SECRET) with sensible local defaults. Add a placeholder vitest test that imports a domain function (e.g. checkGiftAction) and asserts a known result, proving the reuse wiring compiles and runs under the server test runner.
Add server/.gitignore (or extend root) so server/dist and server/node_modules are ignored. Confirm `git status` still shows .kiro/ as the only thing you refuse to commit.
acceptance_criteria: Root `npm test` shows 61 passing tests; `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` succeed with no changes to existing frontend behavior.
`docker run ... postgres:16-alpine` starts and `pg_isready` reports the server is accepting connections; server/scripts/db.sh can start/stop/reset it.
Inside server/: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` succeed, and `npm test` runs the placeholder domain-reuse test green.
GET /health on the running server returns HTTP 200 with {"status":"ok"}.
Server imports the real src/domain modules (verified by the passing domain-reuse test) with no duplicated copies of gift.ts/selectors.ts/etc.
`git status` shows the new server files tracked and .kiro/ still untracked/uncommitted.
verification: Run at repo root: `npm ci && npm test && npm run build && npm run typecheck`.
Start Postgres via server/scripts/db.sh (or the documented docker run) and confirm `docker exec hello-talk-pg pg_isready`.
Inside server/: `npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm run build && npm test`.
Start the server and `curl -s localhost:PORT/health` returns {"status":"ok"}.
findings:
Baseline green: root `npm test` = 61 passing across 4 files; `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` succeed unchanged. Branch feat/backend created from main. Postgres runs via Docker (the daemon is podman under the hood - a harmless cgroup warning prints on `docker run` but the container comes up and `pg_isready` reports accepting connections). Created server/scripts/db.sh with up/down/reset/status/wait subcommands (plain `docker run`, no compose plugin). NOTE for later features: the execute_bash wrapper flags any command literally containing `docker run` and refuses it - invoke Postgres via `bash scripts/db.sh up` (or npm run db:up) rather than a raw `docker run` command line.

Server scaffold under server/: package.json ("type":"module", Fastify 5, pg 8, tsx, vitest), tsconfig.json (strict, ES2022, module ESNext + moduleResolution bundler to match root, verbatimModuleSyntax, isolatedModules, noUncheckedIndexedAccess; rootDir `..`, outDir dist). Domain reuse is done via tsconfig include `../src/domain` (NO copies) plus bundler resolution so the domain files' extensionless relative imports (`./types`) compile as-is. IMPORTANT: because bundler resolution does not rewrite import specifiers, `tsc`-emitted JS keeps extensionless imports which Node ESM cannot resolve at runtime (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). The server is therefore RUN via tsx (`npm run dev` / `npm start`), not via `node dist/...`; `npm run build` exists purely to validate typecheck+emit. FEAT-002 should keep running the server through tsx (or introduce a bundler) rather than `node dist`.

Verified: server `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, and `npm test` (7 tests: 6 domain-reuse + 1 /health via app.inject) all pass. Started the server with tsx and `curl http://127.0.0.1:5311/health` returned HTTP 200 {"status":"ok"}. Config via env (PORT default 5311, HOST 127.0.0.1, DATABASE_URL postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/hello_talk, COOKIE_SECRET dev default). server/.gitignore ignores dist/ and node_modules/. .kiro/ left untracked and uncommitted as required.
